# E0006: invalid escape

Inside a string, `{` starts an interpolation, so a brace is written `\{`. The other escapes are `\n`, `\t`, `\r`, `\0`, `\\`, `\"` and `\u{…}`.

- Rule: [`lexical.escapes`](../../reference/02-lexical.md#lexical.escapes)
- Reported at: the backslash that starts the escape, or the first brace of `{{`.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `syntax` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0006:2
fn braced(x: i64) -> str {
  "{{x}}"
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn braced(x: i64) -> str {
  "\{{x}}"
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0006_invalid_escape.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0006_invalid_escape.lt):

```text
── INVALID ESCAPE ───────────────────────── E0006_invalid_escape.lt:2:4  [E0006]

A brace is written `\{`, not `{{`:

  2 │   "{{x}}"
    │    ^

Inside a string, `{` starts an interpolation, so a brace is written `\{`. The
other escapes are `\n`, `\t`, `\r`, `\0`, `\\`, `\"` and `\u{…}`.

To fix it, write a brace as `\{`:

  2 │   "\{x}"
    │    ~~ ~
```

`stilt check` on [`E0006_swift_interpolation.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0006_swift_interpolation.lt):

```text
── INVALID ESCAPE ─────────────────── E0006_swift_interpolation.lt:3:15  [E0006]

Stilt inserts a value in a string with `{n}`, not `\(n)`:

  3 │   print("n is \(n)")
    │               ^

Every string inserts the value of each `{…}` in it, as `"hello {name}"`.

To fix it, write `{…}`:

  3 │   print("n is {n}")
    │               ~~~
```
